title: Romans teach the just not only may but ought to be firmly persuaded of remission
source_text: XXVI. Porro Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae docent fideles & justos non tantum posse, sed etiam debere de remissione peccatorum suorum, & sua coram Deo justificatione non dubios atque ancipites, sed certo persuasos esse; hancque certitudinem in iis crescere atque augescere, secundum quod in justitia & sanctitate proficiunt: Ideoque ad illorum officium pertinere, ut majorem ac firmiorem indies ea de re certitudinem acquirant: quod fit, dum toto studio in pietate & bonis operibus sese exercent, & in eo animadvertunt clariora & manifestiora divinae adoptionis, & Spiritus Sancti, in se inhabitantis signa. Proinde, si justi nonnulli sibi suadere & confidere non audeant se Deo gratos & acceptos esse, & ab eo in numerum filiorum adoptatos, istud in iis defectum & infirmitatem aliquam arguere. Perfectiores enim, ut jam dixi, solere aliter affectos & dispositos esse, & certam de sua cum Deo reconciliatione fiduciam habere, non vero super eo fluctuare atque ambigere.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover the doctors of the Roman Church teach that the faithful and just not only can but also ought concerning the remission of their sins and their justification before God to be not doubtful and double-minded, but certainly persuaded; and that this certainty grows and increases in them according as they advance in righteousness and holiness: and therefore that it belongs to their duty that they acquire day by day a greater and firmer certainty on that matter—which happens while with all zeal they exercise themselves in piety and good works, and in that observe clearer and more manifest signs of divine adoption and of the Holy Spirit dwelling in them. Accordingly, if some just persons do not dare persuade themselves and trust that they are pleasing and accepted by God and adopted by him into the number of sons, that argues in them some defect and infirmity. For the more perfect, as I have already said, usually are otherwise affected and disposed, and have a certain trust concerning their reconciliation with God, and do not fluctuate and waver over it.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors say the justified ought to be firmly persuaded of pardon, not left in double-mindedness.
Assurance should grow with holiness; inability to trust adoption marks infirmity, not the perfect’s norm.

choices.why: Duty of assurance, not mere permission.
